_about: Editable ScamShield knowledge base. Add phrases, scam types or brands freely. Phrase matching is case-insensitive and matches word starts (so 'suspend' also matches 'suspended').

urgency.label: Artificial urgency
urgency.why: Scammers rush you so you act before thinking or checking with anyone.

threats.label: Threat or fear tactic
threats.why: Threats of lost access, fines or arrest are used to scare you into complying.

financial_request.label: Request for money or payment
financial_request.why: Unexpected requests to send, pay or 'verify' money are the core goal of most scams.

credential_request.label: Request for passwords, OTP, PIN or personal data
credential_request.why: Real organisations never ask you to share OTPs, PINs, passwords or full card details by message or phone.

prize_reward.label: Unexpected prize, refund or reward
prize_reward.why: You can't win a contest you never entered. Fake rewards and refunds are bait.

impersonation.label: Claims to be a bank, government, courier or company
impersonation.why: Scammers borrow the names of trusted organisations to look legitimate.

secrecy_isolation.label: Asks for secrecy
secrecy_isolation.why: Telling you not to talk to anyone stops friends, family or your bank from spotting the scam.

unusual_payment.label: Unusual payment method
unusual_payment.why: Gift cards, crypto, wire transfers and payment apps are hard to reverse, so scammers prefer them.

off_platform.label: Pushes you to another app or channel
off_platform.why: Moving the chat to WhatsApp or Telegram takes you away from platform protections and reporting.

too_good_to_be_true.label: Too-good-to-be-true offer
too_good_to_be_true.why: Guaranteed high returns or easy money for little work are classic scam hooks.

bank_phishing.name: Bank / account phishing
bank_phishing.description: A fake alert pretending to be your bank, card issuer or payment app to steal logins, OTPs or card data.
do_now: Do not click the link or call any number in the message.
Open your bank's official app or type its website address yourself to check for real alerts.
If worried, call the number printed on the back of your card.
do_not: Share OTPs, PINs, CVV or passwords with anyone, including 'bank staff'.
Install any app the sender asks you to install.
if_already_responded: Call your bank immediately and block cards or net banking.
Change your banking password and PIN from a trusted device.
Check recent transactions and report any you don't recognise.

delivery_scam.name: Fake delivery / parcel notice
delivery_scam.description: A text or email about a missed delivery or customs fee that leads to a fake payment or login page.
do_now: Ignore the link. Check the order in the shop's or courier's official app or website.
Compare the tracking number with one from an order you actually placed.
do_not: Pay 'redelivery' or 'customs' fees through a link in a message.
Enter card details on a page you reached from the message.
if_already_responded: Contact your card issuer to block the card and dispute the charge.
Watch for follow-up calls pretending to be your bank.

prize_lottery.name: Prize / lottery / refund scam
prize_lottery.description: You are told you've won something or are owed a refund, but must pay a fee or share details to get it.
do_now: Delete the message. Real prizes don't require upfront fees.
Ask yourself if you actually entered that contest.
do_not: Pay any 'tax', 'fee' or 'courier charge' to receive a prize.
Send ID documents or bank details.
if_already_responded: Stop all contact with the sender.
If you paid, contact your bank or payment app right away and report it.
Watch for repeat 'recovery' scams promising to get your money back for a fee.

job_task_scam.name: Fake job / task scam
job_task_scam.description: Unsolicited job offers with easy pay, often asking you to do small paid tasks, then to deposit your own money.
do_now: Verify the company and recruiter on the company's official careers page.
Treat unsolicited offers of high pay for easy work as a red flag.
do_not: Pay any fee for a job, training or equipment.
Deposit money to 'unlock' tasks or earnings.
if_already_responded: Stop depositing money. Earnings shown in the app are usually fake.
Report the account or group to the platform and to the authorities.

investment_crypto.name: Investment / crypto scam
investment_crypto.description: Promises of guaranteed or very high returns, often via a 'trading expert', fake app or group.
do_now: Remember that guaranteed returns do not exist.
Check whether the firm is registered with your financial regulator.
Talk to someone you trust before moving any money.
do_not: Transfer money to personal accounts or wallets.
Install trading apps from links or unofficial stores.
if_already_responded: Stop sending funds, even if told you must pay fees to withdraw.
Keep screenshots, transaction IDs and wallet addresses as evidence and report them.

romance_scam.name: Romance / relationship scam
romance_scam.description: Someone builds an emotional bond online, then invents an emergency or investment that needs your money.
do_now: Insist on a live video call. Many scammers refuse.
Do a reverse image search on their photos.
Tell a friend or family member about the situation.
do_not: Send money, gift cards or crypto to someone you haven't met in person.
Share intimate photos or ID documents.
if_already_responded: Stop sending money and cut contact.
Report the profile to the platform and keep all chat history as evidence.

tech_support.name: Tech support / remote access scam
tech_support.description: A pop-up, call or message claims your device is infected and pushes you to install remote-access software or pay for fake help.
do_now: Close the pop-up or hang up. Real companies don't cold-call about viruses.
Run a scan with security software you already trust.
do_not: Install AnyDesk, TeamViewer or similar tools at a stranger's request.
Pay with gift cards or give card details.
if_already_responded: Uninstall the remote-access tool and disconnect from the internet.
Change passwords from a clean device and call your bank if you shared financial details.

government_impersonation.name: Government / authority impersonation
government_impersonation.description: Someone claims to be police, customs, tax or a regulator and demands payment or personal data, sometimes threatening arrest.
do_now: Hang up or ignore it. Real agencies don't demand payment by phone, text or gift card.
Call the agency using the official number from its website.
do_not: Stay on a video call because you are told you're under 'digital arrest'. No such legal process exists.
Transfer money to 'verify' or 'clear' yourself.
if_already_responded: Report it immediately to your bank and the cybercrime authorities.
Tell a family member. Isolation is part of this scam.

family_emergency.name: Family / friend emergency scam
family_emergency.description: A message from an unknown number claims to be a relative or friend in trouble and needs money quickly.
do_now: Call the person on their usual number, or ask another relative.
Ask a question only the real person would know.
do_not: Send money based on a text alone.
Keep it secret as the message asks.
if_already_responded: Contact your bank to try to stop or recall the transfer.
Report the number and warn other family members.

marketplace_overpayment.name: Marketplace / overpayment scam
marketplace_overpayment.description: A fake buyer or seller on a classifieds or marketplace site sends a fake payment, asks you to refund the 'extra', or asks you to pay first.
do_now: Meet in person where possible and check the item before paying.
Confirm that money has actually arrived in your account before handing over goods.
do_not: Scan a QR code or approve a collect request to 'receive' money. Receiving money never needs a PIN.
Refund an 'overpayment' before the original payment clears.
if_already_responded: Call your bank or payment app right away to dispute the transaction.
Report the listing and user to the platform.

risk_levels.summary: No strong scam signals found, but that doesn't prove the message is safe.
Some warning signs. Verify through an official channel before acting.
Multiple scam signals. Do not respond, click or pay.
Very likely a scam. Do not engage. Protect your accounts and report it.

do_now: Don't click links, open attachments or call numbers in the message.
Contact the organisation through an official website, app or number you find yourself.
Talk to someone you trust before acting on anything urgent.
do_not: Share OTPs, PINs, passwords or card details.
Send money or gift cards because a message told you to.
if_already_responded: Contact your bank or payment provider right away.
Change passwords for any account you may have exposed.
Keep screenshots and transaction details for your report.

reporting_resources: India: call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in (National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal).
Elsewhere: your bank's fraud team (use the number on your card) and your local police cybercrime unit or national fraud reporting service.
Forward scam texts or emails to the platform or carrier's spam reporting option.
